newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close sharply up, led by financials.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close sharply up, led by financials.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed sharply higher at a three-month high on Monday, led by banking and other financial shares and export manufacturers, brokers said.
The composite index rose 2.12 percent or 14.95 points to 721.20, the highest since February 15 when it hit 722.32.
The market was unmoved by news that four of the Dainong Group's 21 affiliates would be bailed out.
Financial shares rose on speculation that the on-going discussions on financial reforms would make mergers and acquisitions easier, brokers said.
"There was talk that the financial reforms would take shape soon and the talk moved banking stocks," said Kim Young-bum of Seoul Securities.
Bank shares rose despite a lack of developments related to mergers and acquisitions. A presidential commission has been working on measures to reform the nation's financial industry.
The banking sub-index was up 5.51 percent, or 18.90 points, to 362.08. Commercial Bank of Korea gained 310 won to its limit of 4,200 and Korea First Bank rose by 270 won to its limit of 3,690.
Shares in securities firms rose sharply on hopes that the recent rally of the local stock market would help boost earnings of brokerage houses, brokers said.

The industry's sub-index shot up 7.14 percent, or 68.99 points, to 1,035.58. Many brokerages closed at upper limits. Daewoo Securities was up 680 won to 9,300. Hyundai Securities gained 800 won to 11,400.
SEOULBANK said it had decided to bail out Midopa Department Store, Dainong Corp and two unlisted affiliates of the Dainong Group.
Trading in shares of Midopa and Dainong has been suspended since the afternoon session. Midopa last traded at its daily upper limit of 8,140 won, up 600 won, and Dainong at 3,180 won, up 230 won.
SEOULBANK said the decision was in line with an earlier agreement among local banks to prevent promising companies from folding under heavy debts.
